title.narrative: Number of farmers benefitting from effective mechanisms for agricultural extension advice to assist sustainable production growth

description.narrative: A Farmer is a person who cultivates land or crops or raises animals (such as livestock or fish). In PROMOVE Agribiz Program this can be divided into three groups namely:oVulnerable farmers: Smallscale farmers with limited access to means of production (land, water for irrigation, inputs and labor) and limited resilience capacity that can be the cause of negative stress and impact on livelihoods. They strive to produce for personal and family selfconsumption. oSubsistence farmers: Smallscale farmers who predominantly produce crops for family consumption and sell the surplus production to cater for other family needs (health, children, education etc.),oSmallScale farmers: smallscale and marketoriented farmers producing mainly commercial crops to generate income, which is used to respond to family needs.Effective mechanisms for Agricultural Extensive Advice are Participatory extension approaches used to promote agriculture innovations. With participatory extension methods, farmers are involved in problem identification, and the extension agent serves as a facilitator, guiding them through problemsolving strategies.This indicator measures the number of producers receiving technical assistance on Good Agricultural Practices (GAPs) sustainable and resilient practices for crop production and animal husbandry. The support is mainly through Farmer Field School, Farmer Business Schools and mixed public and private extension services provided with support/advice of the Program.

title.narrative: Change (%) on the rate of adoption of quality seed among the Programme beneficiaries

description.narrative: The term seed quality is used in agriculture to describe the overall value of a seed lot for its intended purpose (Hampton, 2002) and includes seed mass, storability, vigor, and germinability. Seed quality describes the potential performance of a seed lot. Trueness to variety; the presence of inert matter, seed of other crops, or weed seed; germination percentage; vigor; appearance; and freedom from disease are important aspects of seed quality. Throughout the Program, the beneficiaries are sensitized to adopt quality seed that will bring better turn over during the harvests. This indicator measures the proportion of beneficiary farmers who utilize certified or quality declared seed for crop production.

description.narrative: Smallholders are microenterprises Enterprises that have commercial objectives and gross sales, as well as less than 25% shareholders from the State or corporate enterprises and are classified by the number of employees as follows: Micro 14, Small 549, and Medium 5090. The indicator measures the number of hactares of farming financed by the program as part of the afforestation schemes.

description.narrative: Micro, Small, Medium Enterprises (MSMEs) are entities that are involved in production, manufacturing and processing of goods and commodities. The concept of MSME was first introduced through the Micro, Small & Medium Enterprises Development (MSMED) Act, 2006 and the enterprises are classified into two divisions:oManufacturing enterprises engaged in the manufacturing or production of goods in any industryoService enterprises engaged in providing or rendering services.In the Mozambique context, Smallholders and MSME are Enterprises that have commercial objectives and gross sales, as well as less than 25% shareholders from the State or corporate enterprises and are classified by the number of employees as follows: Micro 14, Small 549, and Medium 5090. This definition explicitly includes informal microenterprises and smallholder farmers. Regular, formal, or trustbased business linkages are either: Regular formal linkages such as contractual linkages, auctions or cooperative membership. Regular trustbased linkages refer to recurring visits of suppliers, service providers, buyers, trainers to farmers / producers. The indicator will track the smallholders and MSME integrated in supply chains of private companies producing and distributing a specific product or service.

title.narrative: Availability of collaborative IT tools in use

description.narrative: A collaboration tool helps people to collaborate. The purpose of a collaboration tool is to support a group of two or more individuals to accomplish a common goal or objective. Collaboration tools can be either of a nontechnological nature such as paper, flipcharts, postit notes or whiteboards. They can also include software tools and applications such as collaborative software. Collaborative IT tools are technological tools that helps people to collaborate mainly through use of socializing platforms, Teamviews,, Zoom, Google Meet, Whatsapp Groups, Sharepoints Databases etc. To count on this indicator, the collaborative IT tools must be in place, functional and being used. PROMOVE Agribiz will develop collaborative platforms to use both internal and with other Program Implementation Partners

title.narrative: Number of decent jobs created as a result of EU programme support (disaggregated by gender)* PQG

description.narrative: Decent work, a term coined by the International Labour Organization (ILO) in 1999, refers to employment that contributes to the social and economic stability of workers. Social justice values are embedded in decent work, striving for equity and equality beyond the workplace.Decent work is applied to both the formal and informal sector. It must address all kind of jobs, people and families. According to the International Labour Organization (ILO), decent work involves opportunities for work that are productive and deliver a fair income, security in the workplace and social protection for families, better prospects for personal development and social integration, freedom for people to express their concerns, organize and participate in the decisions that affect their lives and equality of opportunity and treatment for all women and men. PROMOVE Agribiz will create jobs through improved access to rural services and improved rural investment climate in the provinces Nampula and Zambzia, thus encouraging more participation of smallholders and MSMEs in economic activities diversification which in turn increase turn over, giving them space for business expansion and human resources absolving. The program will track these jobs created with EU support and calculate the percentage out of all jobs created in the two provinces.

List of nutrition guides typically divide foods into food groups and Recommended Dietary Allowance recommend daily servings of each group for a healthy diet. A balanced diet is made up of foods from at least five food groups: starchy carbohydrates, fruits and vegetables, protein, dairy, and healthy fats. Each provides the range of vitamins and minerals our bodies need to function efficiently. The programme will report this indicator through household surveys. A cohort group of programme women beneficiaries will be asked about the type of meals they had the day before. The calculation will be as follows:Change (%) of women that consume food from five or more of the ten food groups Number of women beneficiaries who had a daily meal that aggregate 5 or more of the food groups the day before / Number of the total women in the survey.
